thread:
lucy: Heads-up — Enterprise deal (Helio Financial) hitting final commit review. They want a 12-month reserved commitment, target steady-state 1.2M inference requests/day mixed chat+generation, avg 300 input+output tokens per request. SLA ask: 99th <350ms. Can SE/infra help sizing and fallback plan?

kevin: TL;DR: need reserved GPUs + autoscale buffer + smaller-model fallback. A few quick questions: what model family are they using in prod? and expected peak concurrency?

lucy: They plan to use our recommended mid-large model (6-12B), but open to quantized variants. Peak concurrency estimated ~1.8x steady (so ~2.16M req/day peak window). Business wants cost predictability for commit pricing.

raj: Quick calc notes: assume avg 300 tokens, generation ~200 tokens per request. Measured throughput examples on our infra: one A100-80 yields ~120 req/s for 512-token generation with batching (q=4). For 200 tokens avg, conservatively ~160 req/s per GPU with batching.

kevin: Using raj's number: steady 1.2M/day = 13.9 req/s average. Peak 1.8x => 25 req/s sustained over peak window. That is ~0.16 GPUs steady at peak; but GPUs are indivisible and we need headroom for SLOs and warmup. Recommend a baseline reserved pool of 2 GPUs (hot) for low-latency + autoscale up to 12 GPUs for traffic spikes.

maria: Pricing context — current list reserved A100 equiv = $9,500/month/GPU (example), billed against commit. Need to show two scenarios: conservative (2 reserved) vs runway (6 reserved + burst).

kevin: Autoscale policy draft (suggested):
```
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 12
  metric: requests_per_second
  target_per_replica: 140
  scale_up_cooldown: 30s
  scale_down_cooldown: 180s
  prewarm_threshold: 0.6  # start prewarming when target > 60%
```
This targets ~140 req/s per GPU which is conservative for mixed workloads and gives room for KV cache and batching variability.

kevin: Also recommend a hedged prewarm pool (burst credits) of 2 GPUs that can spin up faster with warm KV caches (keep them in standby container state). That reduces 99th tail during spikes.

lucy: On fallback — they require guaranteed availability. Can we add an automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model if latency breaches 99th for >5m?

raj: Yes — route policy can fallback to compatible quantized variant (same tokenizer/state) and limit output length/prompt features. Typical config:
```
fallbacks:
  - condition: p99_latency > 350ms for 5m
    action: route_to_model: quantized-6b
    max_tokens_override: 150
    note: reduce generation to preserve throughput
```
This keeps service up while reducing per-request compute.

emily: For POC we should propose a 2-week burst test: reserve 2 GPUs + autoscale to 6, run synthetic peak windows, capture p50/p95/p99 and cost delta. I'll include that in the POA to the customer.

maria: For commit pricing options to present:
- Option A (conservative): 2 reserved GPUs, nightly prewarm, autoscale to 6 — commit discount X%.
- Option B (runway): 6 reserved GPUs, burst credits 4, autoscale to 12 — higher commit, deeper discount, SLA add-on.
Include expected monthly cost table (I'll prepare offline).

kevin: Ops checklist for POC:
- @raj: create reserved pool 2x A100 equiv in prod region, configure autoscale policy above.
- @kevin: create canary route with fallback and telemetry hooks (p99 alerts).
- @maria: draft pricing scenarios + estimated monthly spend and unit economics.
- @emily/@lucy: confirm test windows and synthetic load profile.

capacity-bot: reserved_pool created: pool-id rp-helio-poc, size=2, region=us-west-2 (dry-run).

raj: I'll spin up the reserved pool tomorrow morning and attach a canary route. Will also enable KV cache warmers. Expect initial logs in the console.

lucy: Great — I'll send the POC proposal to the customer after we have the cost table. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

kevin: One more note — recommend a 20% commit headroom in proposal to avoid forced scale during growth. Means present numbers as "committed + recommended buffer" so finance/ procurement can see runway.

lucy: Ack. Action items noted. I'll update the sheet and ping when ready for customer call.
